text: 作为妇女之友，欢场华佗，我先表个态，我们要坚定不移地尊崇宪法，学习宪法、遵守宪法、维护宪法、警钟长鸣，居然有一小撮儿人试图将卖淫合法化，简直是痴心妄想，想入非非，飞禽走兽，寿与天齐，其乐无穷，当然，后两句是开玩笑。
en: As a friend to women and the Hua Tuo of the pleasure quarters, let me first state my position: we must unwaveringly revere the constitution, study it, abide by it, uphold it, and keep the alarm bell ringing. Yet a tiny handful of people are trying to legalise prostitution — it is sheer wishful thinking, wild fantasy, like birds and beasts sharing a lifespan with the heavens, with endless delight. Of course, those last two phrases were a joke.

text: 人这一辈子会遇见很多问题，我们不能单一地看待问题表象，更不能抛开时代和社会背景，就像老黑头儿说的存在即合理，很多事情没有对错，甚至没有定论，仅仅是时代下的一个符号，所以，遇见问题没必要非得反驳，如果非得反驳，您不妨先看看这个问题是如何形成的。
en: Over a lifetime one meets many problems. We must not view the surface of a problem in isolation, still less set aside its era and social context. As Old Black-head says, what exists is rational; many things are neither right nor wrong, not even settled — they are merely a symbol of their time. So there is no need to argue back when you meet a problem; if you must rebut, you might first look at how the problem came to be.

text: 说到卖淫，世界各地都存在这种商业行为，这也是一个古老的职业。
en: Speaking of prostitution, this commercial activity exists all over the world, and it is also an ancient profession.

text: 可任何职业，除了瘾头儿大的，都是以温饱为主。
en: Yet in any trade, save for those with a serious habit, the chief aim is simply to feed and clothe oneself.

text: 既在江湖内，便是苦命人。
en: Once you are in the jianghu, you are a soul bound to a hard life.

text: 众所周知，中国最早的妓院可以追溯到春秋时期，管仲是这行儿的祖师爷，‘宫中七市，女閭七百，国人非之，以佐军兴，皆寡妇也。
en: As everyone knows, China's earliest brothels can be traced back to the Spring and Autumn period; Zhong Guan is the founding patron of this trade. ‘Within the palace were seven markets, and seven hundred houses of women; the common people disapproved, yet it was done to aid the army's provisions, and all were widows."

text: 您瞧瞧，无论是为了税收，还是服务军队，这个行业是在国家的指导下而诞生。
en: Just look — whether for taxation or to serve the army, this industry was born under the guidance of the state.

text: 行业有了，制度也会愈加完善，比如妓女要登记体检，有专人管理，客人也得守规矩，随后又有了青楼，今天很多文学影视作品并不负责任，把青楼和妓院混为一谈，表现成低俗放荡无知的所在，其实不然，青楼并不是脱了裤子就上炕，妓院也没有当街拉拉扯扯，那是政商两界，文人墨客，乡绅富贾的聚集地。
en: Once the industry existed, the system grew ever more refined: prostitutes had to register and have medical examinations, with dedicated overseers, and patrons had to obey the rules. Later came the qinglou. Many literary and film works today are irresponsible, conflating the qinglou with the brothel and portraying them as vulgar, debauched and ignorant places. In fact it was not so: the qinglou was not a matter of dropping one's trousers and climbing onto the kang, nor did brothels drag people about in the street. They were gathering places for the political and commercial worlds, for men of letters, and for local gentry and wealthy merchants.

text: 青楼不仅是高档消费场所，还有门槛儿，姑娘们都受过训，卖艺不卖身，主要服务于士大夫阶层，过去讲究万般皆下品，唯有读书高，您不光要有钱，还得识字，而老百姓过得清苦，就没几个识字的，自然没条件去附庸风雅，就像改革开放后的首批娱乐城，老百姓一个月赚几百块钱，根本没钱去消费，只有领导，大老板，大流氓可以去得起。
en: The qinglou was not only a high-end venue but had a threshold to entry; the girls were all trained, selling their art but not their bodies, serving mainly the scholar-official class. In the past it was said that all trades were base and only study was noble — you needed not merely money but literacy. Common folk lived in straitened circumstances and few could read, so naturally they had no means to pose as men of refinement. It was like the first entertainment cities after reform and opening-up: a common labourer earned a few hundred yuan a month and simply could not afford to spend there; only leaders, big bosses and great ruffians could.

text: 原来的制度又允许三妻六妾，权贵们不缺性资源，物质得到满足后，追求的是精神生活，是爱情，就像现在某些绅士，去了一趟夜总会看了两场直播就以为姑娘爱上他了一样，被迷得七荤八素，兜儿都掏裂了一个道理。
en: The old system also permitted three wives and six concubines; the powerful lacked no sexual resources. Once material needs were met, what they pursued was spiritual life, was love — much like certain gentlemen nowadays who visit a nightclub, watch two livestreams, and fancy the girl has fallen for them, becoming utterly spellbound, their pockets turned inside out — the same principle.

text: 封建社会推崇愚忠愚孝，父母之命，媒妁之言，只要父母看上了，门当户对，婚事就成了，掀盖头的那一刻才见着媳妇面儿不新鲜，好与坏全凭媒婆儿一张嘴，老话说，嫁鸡随鸡，嫁狗随狗，嫁个木头您抱着走，是相对的，而青楼的存在正好儿弥补了这个痛点，姑娘都是窈窕淑女，对相对看，还通文墨，风花雪月信手拈来，历史上那些至死不渝的爱情，大部分出自这里。
en: The feudal society prized blind loyalty and blind filial piety — the command of parents and the words of matchmakers. So long as the parents approved and the families were well matched, the marriage was settled; seeing one's bride only at the lifting of the veil was nothing new, and whether she was good or bad rested entirely on the matchmaker's tongue. As the old saying goes, marry a chicken and follow the chicken, marry a dog and follow the dog, marry a log and carry it in your arms — it was a matter of fate. The existence of the qinglou happened to mend this sore point: its girls were all graceful ladies, pleasing to behold and literate besides, effortlessly versed in romance and poetry. Most of those love stories faithful unto death in history sprang from here.

text: 妓院也分三六九等，小班、茶室、下处、还有属于穷人的暗门子。
en: Brothels, too, were ranked into grades: the small houses, the tea rooms, the lower lodgings, and the hidden doors belonging to the poor.

text: 头等的小班也了不得，那姑娘都得有老妈子伺候着，想吃什么可以点菜，行动坐卧，举手投足，必须有规矩有深沉，会得也多，琴棋书画，吟诗作对，能歌善舞，说学逗唱，十八般兵器，总得有两样儿拿得出手的绝活儿，不是说街面儿上随便找个大傻丫头，一问三不知，又缺嘴，自己能干五碗大米饭，人家出个上联儿，日照香炉生紫烟，她撑得嗝儿嘎的，拍拍肚子，我想上趟洗手间，那主顾凭什么花钱，一脚就得踹出去。
en: The top-grade small houses were something else: the girls all had maidservants attending them, could order dishes to eat, and in every movement — sitting, standing, gesture — had to observe strict decorum and depth. They had many skills: zither, chess, calligraphy and painting; composing poetry and matching couplets; singing and dancing; comic routines; and among the eighteen weapons of martial arts, they had to have at least a couple of impressive specialties. It was not a matter of grabbing some silly girl off the street who knows nothing when asked, has a harelip, and can put away five bowls of rice by herself. When someone offers the couplet 'the sunlit censer breathes forth purple mist', she, bloated and belching, pats her belly and says she wants to pop to the lavatory — why would a customer pay for that? He would kick her straight out.

text: 所以说，能干这行儿的不是一般人，只不过命不一样罢了。
en: So those who could work this trade were no ordinary people; it is only that their fates differed.

text: 要想和姑娘云雨一番，也没影视剧演的那么容易，您得先交盘子钱，说好听点儿就是茶钱，逢年过节来捧场，大把的花钱，就像现在的主播一样，要不然领家儿妈妈，杈杆儿，伙计，老妈子，厨子，这一大帮人吃谁去啊。
en: To share cloud and rain with a girl was not as easy as the films show. You first had to pay the tray fee — politely called the tea fee — and come to show support at festivals, spending freely, much like today's livestreamers; otherwise, who would feed the madam, the pimp, the servants, the maids, the cook — that whole crowd?

text: 重要的是，无论青楼还是妓院，都是符合市场需求的存在。
en: What matters is that both the qinglou and the brothel were existences that answered the market's demand.

text: 在穷人眼里，它可以是最低级最原始的泄欲场所；在富人眼里，它可以是寻欢作乐，行贿受贿的媒介；在顶级阶层眼里，它可以是策划谋反，牵线搭桥的不二选择；在文人眼里，它可以是追求精神满足的乐园，灵感如泉涌，一字一句，一喘一息，一进一出，都在为唐诗宋词添砖加瓦。
en: In the eyes of the poor, it could be the lowest, most primitive outlet for desire; in the eyes of the rich, a medium for pleasure-seeking and for bribery and graft; in the eyes of the top stratum, the unrivalled choice for plotting rebellion and pulling strings; in the eyes of men of letters, a paradise for pursuing spiritual fulfilment, where inspiration gushed like a spring, and every word and line, every breath and gasp, every entrance and exit, added bricks and tiles to the Tang poetry and Song lyrics.

text: 很多时候，大家对过去的固有印象是封建，传统，保守，实际则不然，咱们既有男女授受不亲的思想，也允许青楼妓院的存在，两者似乎并不冲突，就拿我们北京来说，万历年间，意大利传教士利玛窦见识到了这里如何吃鸭子，玩鸭子，连夜给教会写信，陈述了同性恋的情况，以及饲养娈童等问题，要知道，这些都是被教会所不耻，要被烧死的异端。
en: Much of the time, people's fixed impression of the past is feudal, traditional, conservative — but in truth it was not so. We held the belief that men and women should not touch in giving and receiving, yet also permitted the existence of qinglou and brothels; the two seemed not to conflict. Take our Beijing, for instance: during the Wanli reign, the Italian missionary Matteo Ricci witnessed how men here kept and played with 'ducks' [male prostitutes], and wrote overnight to the Church describing the situation of homosexuality and the keeping of catamites. Bear in mind these were things the Church held in contempt — heresies to be burnt at the stake.

text: 白云苍狗，沧海桑田，异端没烧死，八国联军倒是来了，烧杀淫掠，无恶不作，我有理由怀疑当初那封信的内容，为什么时至今日，教会，神父，很多都成了信中人。
en: White clouds turn to grey dogs, the sea becomes farmland; the heretics were not burnt, but the Eight-Nation Alliance came instead, burning, killing, raping and plundering, committing every conceivable evil. I have reason to doubt the contents of that letter — why is it that to this day, the Church and the priests have themselves become men of the faith?

text: 随着历史的车轮滚滚向前，同样是因为市场，青楼消亡，妓院的质量和数量骤减，那时候正赶上封建社会结束，意识形态发生巨变，老百姓知道了什么叫压迫和剥削，开始提倡民主，人权，自由，批判旧社会的制度与陋习。
en: As the wheel of history rolled forward, it was again because of the market that the qinglou vanished and the quality and number of brothels plummeted. This coincided with the end of feudal society and a great shift in ideology; common people learned what oppression and exploitation meant, began to champion democracy, human rights and freedom, and to criticise the institutions and vices of the old society.

text: 可光批判也没用，有利益的地方就有江湖，妓院依然存在。
en: Yet criticism alone was useless; wherever there is interest, there is jianghu, and the brothels remained.

text: 不仅存在，像上海这样的国际大都市，地理位置，政治意义，比较特殊，有港口，有租界，有洋鬼子，有华侨，夜夜笙歌，名妓，名媛，交际花，数不胜数。
en: Not only did they remain, but in an international metropolis like Shanghai, with its special geographical position and political significance — ports, concessions, foreign devils, overseas Chinese — there were singing and revelry every night, and famed courtesans, celebrated beauties and socialites without number.

text: 没办法，夜生活越丰富的地方，经济越好，这是毋庸置疑的事实。
en: There is no help for it: the richer the nightlife of a place, the stronger its economy — an indisputable fact.

text: 民国初年到新中国成立期间，政局动荡，战乱不断，民不聊生，底层老百姓吃不饱，大量涌入城市，把媳妇儿孩子卖到妓院很正常，地痞流氓，人贩子，军警，各方势力都可以分一杯羹，也不光是这行儿，艺人也一样，甭管男女，让有势力的主顾看上了，比如遗老遗少，公公，军阀，汉奸，特务，那就不光是卖嗓子了。
en: From the early Republic of China to the founding of New China, the political scene was turbulent, war raged without cease, and the people could not live in peace. The lowest folk went hungry and poured into the cities in great numbers; selling one's wife and children to a brothel was quite normal. Local bullies, human traffickers, military and police, and all manner of powers could take a cut. And it was not only this trade — entertainers were the same: regardless of sex, once a powerful patron took a fancy — say a leftover Qing loyalist, a eunuch, a warlord, a collaborator, an agent — it was no longer only a matter of selling one's voice.

text: 要说真正取缔妓院，还得是解放后，毛主席怹一句话，什么叫八大胡同，小白楼，哪个又叫十里秦淮，十里洋场，全都洗心革面，重新做人，先看病，跟着就安排工作，与此同时，作家，编剧，导演，宣传部门，也开始口诛笔伐旧社会的黑暗，妓女现身说法，句句血泪，惨绝人寰。
en: If we speak of truly abolishing brothels, that had to wait until after liberation. At Chairman Mao's word, what were the Ba Da Hu Tong, the Xiao Bai Lou, what were the Shi Li Qin Huai, the Shi Li Yang Chang — all washed their hearts and renewed themselves, becoming new people. First they were treated for illness, then given work. At the same time, writers, screenwriters, directors and the propaganda department began to condemn the darkness of the old society in speech and in print; the prostitutes spoke from their own experience, every word soaked in blood and tears, utterly tragic.

text: 新中国成立后，百废待兴，美帝苏修虎视眈眈，咱们依然是落后的国家。
en: After the founding of New China, everything lay in ruins awaiting renewal; American imperialists and Soviet revisionists looked on with covetous eyes, and we remained a backward country.

text: 要改变，要发展，要强大，怎么办？
en: To change, to develop, to grow strong — what was to be done?

text: 一九七九年，那是一个春天，有一位老人，在中国的南海边画了一个圈，自此，改革开放的春风吹遍了祖国大地，计划经济的时代结束了，允许一部分人先富起来。
en: In 1979, it was a spring; an old man drew a circle on the southern shore of China, and from then on the spring breeze of reform and opening-up swept across the motherland. The era of the planned economy ended, and some were allowed to get rich first.

text: 邓公英明，怹说过，不管黑猫白猫，能捉老鼠的就是好猫，怹也准确的预见到了，改革开放打开了窗户，新鲜空气会进来，苍蝇蚊子也会飞进来。
en: Deng Xiaoping was wise; he said that whether a cat is black or white, the one that catches mice is a good cat. He also accurately foresaw that reform and opening-up would open the window: fresh air would come in, but so would flies and mosquitoes.

text: 那会儿，全国一盘棋，每天都在发生翻天覆地的变化。
en: At that time the whole nation moved as one chessboard, and earth-shaking changes happened every day.

text: 可面对时代的红利，有些人胆子大，抓住了机会，吃得满嘴流油，而更多的老百姓还沉浸在铁饭碗时代，老实巴交了一辈子，到头儿来，还没纳过闷儿呢，被下岗了。
en: Yet facing the dividends of the era, some with nerve seized the chance and feasted greasily, while more common folk were still immersed in the age of the iron rice bowl, having been honest all their lives, and before they had even come to their senses, they were laid off.

text: 她们怎么办，不能偷，也不能抢，更不能去反对些什么。
en: What were they to do? They could not steal, could not rob, still less oppose anything.

text: 当然，大部分人还是扛了下来，靠出卖劳动力，起早贪黑，勉强糊口。
en: Of course, most endured, selling their labour, rising early and working late, barely scraping by.

text: 这个世界，家家有本难念的经，有人等着米下锅，等着给孩子交学费，床上躺着受了工伤的丈夫，没有任何赚钱能力，老人也需要赡养，尤其是看着从外地打工回来的邻居，朋友，姐妹，摇身一变，穿金戴银，崩溃就在一瞬间，接下来的路怎么走，生活已经替她们做出了选择。
en: This world — every family has its own scripture hard to recite. Some wait for rice to cook, wait to pay their children's school fees; a husband lies in bed with a work injury, unable to earn; elderly parents need support. Especially when they watch neighbours, friends and sisters who returned from labouring elsewhere undergo a sudden transformation, decked in gold and silver — the collapse comes in an instant. As for the road ahead, life has already chosen it for them.

text: 彼时，北方有大量妇女南下，而南方的妇女继续南下，到了南洋。
en: At that time, large numbers of women from the north went south, and the women of the south continued south, reaching Nanyang.

text: 不占地，不占房，工作只要一张床；不生女，不生男，不给政府添麻烦；无噪声，无污染，只是偶尔喊一喊；不集资，不贷款，自带设备搞发展；下岗妹，不流泪，就业自己找机会；不逃税，不欠费，挣多挣少无所谓；不嫌脏，不怕累，拉动内需创外汇；不怕打，不怕捶，坚决不说陪过谁。
en: Take no land, take no rooms, the work needs only a bed; bear no daughters, bear no sons, give the government no trouble; no noise, no pollution, just the occasional shout; no collecting funds, no loans, bring your own kit to develop; laid-off sisters, shed no tears, find your own employment; pay taxes, owe no fees, earn much or little, it is all the same; disdain no dirt, fear no toil, stimulate domestic demand and earn foreign exchange; fear no beating, fear no pounding, resolutely never say who you have kept company with.

text: 这是戏谑，是自嘲，也是无奈。
en: This is banter, self-mockery, and also helplessness.

text: 短短数载，卖淫死灰复燃，却也是符合规律的必然结果。
en: In just a few years, prostitution flared up again from the ashes — yet it was also the inevitable result in keeping with the laws at work.

text: 说起来，卖淫嫖娼就像过去的拉帮套，你可以说它是陋习，是畸形的婚姻状态，但不可否认它的存在，以及存在价值。
en: Speaking of it, prostitution and whoring are like the old 'pulling the trace' arrangement of the past — you may call it a bad custom, a deformed state of marriage, but its existence, and its value in existing, cannot be denied.

text: 中国高速发展的黄金时代，多少暗箱操作的审批，多少低买高卖，多少贷款，多少高楼大厦，都是在晕乎乎白花花黑洞洞中签的字。
en: During China's golden age of rapid development, how many approvals behind closed doors, how many buy-low-sell-high deals, how many loans, how many skyscrapers — all signed in a dizzy, pallid, pitch-dark haze.

text: 虽然违规，不合法，但是效率很快。
en: Though it broke the rules and was unlawful, it was efficient and fast.

text: 现在常说速度，咱们用短短几十年的时间，走完了发达国家几百年走过的工业化路程。
en: People often speak of speed nowadays: in just a few decades we completed the industrialisation journey that took developed nations centuries.

text: 没有人能否定改革开放的伟大，同样，也要接受其弊端。
en: No one can deny the greatness of reform and opening-up; equally, one must accept its drawbacks.

text: 中国地大物博，哪怕是在二十一世纪的今天，我们还有很长的路要走。
en: China is vast in territory and abundant in resources; even today in the twenty-first century, we still have a long road ahead.

text: 很多人觉得，从初代下海的老姐姐，到现在的外围，假名媛，解决温饱早就不成问题了，送个外卖都能活着，更多的年轻人是爱慕虚荣，好吃懒做，想捞偏门，这个问题确实存在，但您也不能光说剥削与压迫，人权与自由，甚至卖淫就该死，还要考虑教育问题，经济问题，地域问题，到底是什么在冲击着年轻人的感官。
en: Many feel that from the first generation of 'sea-entering' older sisters to today's peripheral girls and fake socialites, mere subsistence is long since solved — you can survive delivering takeaway. More young people are vain, lazy and greedy, wanting to fish in troubled waters. This problem does indeed exist, but you cannot only talk of exploitation and oppression, human rights and freedom, or even that prostitutes deserve death; you must also consider education, the economy and regional issues — what exactly is assailing the young people's senses.

text: 浮躁的社会环境，金钱至上的观念，还是面对生存的无奈？
en: A restless social environment, the notion that money is supreme, or the helplessness of facing survival?

text: 相信我，没人想卖淫，也并不是谁都可以衣食无忧。
en: Believe me, no one wants to prostitute themselves, and not everyone can live free of care for food and clothing.

text: 有套房子，父母双全，在自己走投无路时伸出援手，再正常不过了，而现实太残酷，这些是很多人的梦，渴望而不可及。
en: To have a flat, both parents alive, and a helping hand when one is at one's wits' end — that is only natural; yet reality is too cruel, and these are the dreams of many, longed for but out of reach.

text: 中国的治安环境在全世界屈指可数，早就没了旧社会的残忍，更有法律支持妇女权益，只要不是组织者，卖淫不是重罪，卫生环境也有了极大提升，性病轻易不能致死了，所以，卖淫这条路，也许就是她们眼中的自由与权利。
en: China's public security environment is among the very best in the world; the cruelty of the old society is long gone, and there are laws upholding women's rights. So long as one is not an organiser, prostitution is not a grave crime, the sanitary environment has greatly improved, and venereal disease can no longer easily kill. Thus, the path of prostitution may well be, in their eyes, freedom and a right.

text: 您冲她们恶语相加，咬牙切齿，倒是没问题，她们出来混，就得承担后果，挨骂也正常，但您也得考虑，是不是骂错方向了？
en: You curse them and gnash your teeth — that is fine; they are in this game and must bear the consequences, so being scolded is normal. But you should also consider: are you cursing in the wrong direction?

text: 邓公当年说，允许一部分人先富起来，还有后半句呢，先富要带动后富。
en: Deng Xiaoping said back then that some might be allowed to get rich first — but there is a second half: the first to grow rich must bring along those who come after.

text: 怎奈群众和干部里有坏人，先富不但没带动后富，还把国有资产私分，贱卖，变成了私有资产，造成大批工人下岗，更有甚者私吞安置费，这帮孙子光天化日吃着人血馒头，把财产和孩子转移到了国外，更可怕的是，当资本的巨兽慢慢长大，工人阶级陷入了被压榨与剥削的无限循环。
en: Yet among the masses and the cadres there were bad people; the first rich not only failed to bring along the later rich, but privately divided up state assets, selling them cheap and turning them into private property, throwing large numbers of workers out of work. Worse still, some embezzled the resettlement funds; these bastards, in broad daylight, ate steamed buns soaked in human blood, transferring their wealth and children abroad. More terrifying still, as the giant beast of capital slowly grew, the working class fell into an endless cycle of being squeezed and exploited.

text: 到底是谁背叛了工人阶级？
en: In the end, who betrayed the working class?

text: 太多苍白无力地呐喊就像操你妈，往往说得出，却做不到。
en: Too many pallid, powerless shouts are like 'fuck your mother' — often said, but never done.

text: 当年工人阶级风光无限，敢与全世界的资本家为敌，他们无畏牺牲，打退了美帝，拿下了汉城，红军开着坦克攻占了柏林，在国会大厦升起了第一面红旗，红场上震耳欲聋的乌拉犹在耳边，可他们怎么也想不到，自己的后代再次挤破脑袋前往资本主义国家，不再是为了英特纳雄耐尔，而是卖淫，变成了消费品，唯一值得欣慰的就是国外赚钱国内花，也算是曲线救国了。
en: In those years the working class was glorious beyond measure, daring to make enemies of capitalists the world over; they feared no sacrifice, drove back the American imperialists, took Seoul, and the Red Army drove its tanks to capture Berlin, raising the first red flag over the Reichstag; the deafening 'Hurrah' on Red Square still rings in the ear. Yet they could never have imagined that their descendants would again crowd and scramble to reach capitalist countries — no longer for the Internationale, but to prostitute themselves, becoming consumer goods. The only comfort is that they earn abroad and spend at home, which counts, in a roundabout way, as saving the nation.

text: 达瓦里氏，如果有人问你列宁格勒和斯大林格勒在哪儿。
en: Tovarishch, if someone asks you where Leningrad and Stalingrad are.

text: 你还找得到吗？
en: Can you still find them?

text: 值得玩味的是，将卖淫合法的地区和国家，往往是崇尚人权的发达国家，而从业人员最多的却是来自另一个阵营的发展中国家。
en: What is worth pondering is that the regions and countries that legalise prostitution tend to be developed nations that champion human rights, yet the great majority of those who work in it come from developing countries of the other camp.

text: 其实这个问题算是老生常谈了，往年就有人大代表提过合法化的建议，到底利大于弊，还是弊大于利，可我们心中的答案不重要，支持与反对，它都存在。
en: In fact this question is a tired old one; in past years an NPC deputy has even proposed legalisation. Whether the benefits outweigh the harms or the harms the benefits — our answer in our hearts does not matter; with or without support and opposition, it exists.

text: 不过可以肯定的是，从国家利益的层面上看，卖淫就不能合法化。
en: What can be affirmed, however, is that from the standpoint of national interest, prostitution cannot be legalised.

text: 试想一下，现在都鼓励要二胎了，您本身就买不起房，结不起婚，养不起孩子，跟个造粪机似的，一点儿贡献没有，好家伙，这回卖淫合法化了，可以合理合法的解决性需求，您吃着垃圾食品，玩儿着GTA，刚按完喇叭，诱人的声音与画面如此逼真，您掏出手机找到滴滴打炮，直接叫上门儿服务，完事儿点一根儿烟，再压一口冰镇可乐。
en: Just imagine: now we are even encouraged to have a second child, yet you yourself cannot afford a flat, a marriage or a child, like a mere manure-making machine contributing nothing. Well then — this time prostitution is legalised, and your sexual needs can be met reasonably and lawfully. You eat junk food, play GTA, just honked the horn, and the tempting sound and image are so lifelike; you pull out your phone, find Didi Da Pao, and call the service straight to your door; when done, you light a cigarette and take a swig of iced cola.

text: 姐妹们也如是，现在很多独立女性，要不是图片刻欢愉，根本不需要男人，赶上点儿背，遇到个渣男，简直就是自己人生的绊脚石。
en: The sisters are the same: many independent women today need men not at all, save for a moment's pleasure; if they are unlucky and meet a scumbag, he is simply a stumbling block in their own lives.

text: 到时候，男女都一样，姐妹们也能找。
en: By then, men and women alike, the sisters can seek them out too.

text: 下班回家，挑个从业者放松，先看看介绍，会什么绝活儿，有什么评论，完事儿赶紧让他走，自己踏踏实实舒舒服服睡一觉。
en: After work, go home, pick a practitioner to relax with; first read the profile — what specialty they have, what reviews — then when done send them off quickly and sleep soundly and comfortably yourself.

text: 您的小家倒是美了，大家怎么办啊？
en: Your little household may be lovely, but what of the greater household?

text: 卖淫能不能合法，是很简单的算术题，是为了那点儿税收，还是让您结婚，生孩子，买房子，按部就班，哪个能利益最大化呢？
en: Whether prostitution can be legalised is a simple sum: is it for that bit of tax revenue, or to have you marry, bear children, buy a flat and follow the proper order — which maximises interest?

text: 如果抛开国家利益，从个人利益出发，反对卖淫合法化最多的肯定是姐妹们，毕竟，男性嫖娼占了大多数，破坏了感情，甚至婚姻。
en: If we set aside national interest and start from personal interest, the ones who most oppose legalising prostitution must surely be the sisters — after all, men make up the majority of clients, and it ruins feelings and even marriages.

text: 这点我是坚决支持的，男人可以风流，不能下流，更不能对家庭不负责任。
en: This I firmly support: a man may be romantically free, but not base, and still less irresponsible to his family.

text: 可现实生活中，通奸比嫖娼的危害和影响更大，往往两败俱伤。
en: Yet in real life, adultery does greater harm and has a greater effect than whoring, often leaving both sides wounded.

text: 老话说得好，赌尽盗，奸尽杀。
en: As the old saying goes well: gambling ends in theft, adultery ends in murder.

text: 通奸会日久生情，付出了时间，精力，金钱，并且不带保护措施，有交叉感染的风险，更是让无数家庭支离破碎，成了离婚的导火索。
en: Adultery breeds affection over time; one invests time, energy and money, and often without protection, risking cross-infection — and it shatters countless families, becoming the fuse for divorce.

text: 我们经常看到，当妻子抓到男人嫖娼时，无论是出于家庭还是孩子的原因，有很大一部分人选择了原谅，属于人民内部矛盾，但抓小三儿时，就属于敌我矛盾了，妻子带着兄弟姐妹，严刑拷打，老虎凳，辣椒水儿，恨不得蘸点儿芥末，好好刷刷对方的扇贝，完事儿还得撒把盐沙沙水。
en: We often see that when a wife catches her man whoring, for the sake of family or children a great many choose forgiveness — a contradiction among the people. But catching the 'other woman' is a contradiction between enemy and self: the wife brings brothers and sisters, subjects her to harsh torture — the tiger bench, pepper water — and would fain dip in some mustard to give the other's scallop a good scrub, then sprinkle salt to 'sand' the water.

text: 这也是古代为什么要把通奸入刑的原因。
en: This is also why in antiquity adultery was made a criminal offence.

text: 怎奈法律变了，窃钩者诛，窃国者诸侯。
en: Yet the law has changed: he who steals a hook is put to death, while he who steals a state becomes a feudal lord.

text: 新闻上常演，某某贪官罪行累累，通常还要加上一条包养众多情妇，最严重的罪名是对组织不忠，道德问题从来就不是什么大事儿，可我觉得那些一屁股坐上升殖器把自己包装成人民公仆的人还没有妓女值得尊敬，对老百姓的伤害也更大，虽然本质都是卖，但人家卖的高级，卖的骄傲，卖的光宗耀祖，自此摇身一变，满嘴仁义道德，严抓严打卖淫嫖娼。
en: The news often shows how some corrupt official, with countless crimes, usually has added the charge of keeping many mistresses; the most serious accusation is disloyalty to the organisation, while moral issues were never a great matter. Yet I think those who plant their backside on a rising penis and package themselves as public servants are less worthy of respect than prostitutes, and do greater harm to ordinary folk. Though the essence is all 'selling', they sell at a higher level, sell with pride, sell to the glory of their ancestors; then with a flip they are transformed, mouths full of benevolence and morality, strictly cracking down on prostitution and whoring.

text: 至此，我们的支持与反对，赞成与反驳，并没什么用，千百年过去了，法律就在那里，卖淫的人也在，没有谁能改变这个事实。
en: By now, our support and opposition, our approval and rebuttal, are of no use. A thousand years have passed; the law is there, and so are those who prostitute themselves — no one can change this fact.

text: 你我皆凡人，人微言轻，轻轻地来轻轻地走。
en: You and I are both mortal; our words carry little weight. We come gently and go gently.

text: 所以，当我们谈论卖淫该不该合法的时候我们在谈论什么？
en: So, when we talk about whether prostitution should be legal, what are we talking about?
